gap: No result ChatGPT got states which 3 kWh units can be bought and shipped today: on 2026-11-27 the Jackery HomePower 3000 (ChatGPT's pick) reads unavailable on jackery.com, the Anker SOLIX F3000 reads Sold Out with a 3-7 week ship notice, the Pecron F3000LFP is a pre-order shipping mid-December, and the BLUETTI Elite 300 now ships from Dec 28 (ChatGPT said Dec 14), while the EcoFlow DELTA 3000 Gen4 ($1,299) and Dabbsson 3000L ($969) read as available.
standout_why: Compared against powerstations.reviews/jackery-3000, power-verdict.com best-3000wh, wattpowerstation.com home-backup guide, thepowerstationreport.com and thesolarlab.com big-stations (all opened 2026-11-27). powerstations.reviews has dated prices (Nov 2-23) and marks three other models sold out, but shows no availability note for the HomePower 3000, F3000, Elite 300 or F3000LFP and has no DELTA 3000 Gen4 row. power-verdict says its prices 'come from an earlier reading' and gives no ship dates. The other three give no availability or ship dates. None carries a same-day price and ship status for every unit in the class.
decides: It changes the pick. Three of ChatGPT's four named units cannot ship now from their makers, and the fourth (Elite 300) ships Dec 28, which is 31 days out and past the four-week limit for a pick. Among units reading as available today, the Dabbsson 3000L is cheapest at $969 (3,000 W) and the EcoFlow DELTA 3000 Gen4 at $1,299 is the cheapest with 3,600 W. Of ours, Nature's Generator L3600 ($1,399.99), Mango Power E ($1,499) and Growatt HELIOS 3600 ($1,589) read as available. The Elite 300 stays the price pick only if its Amazon listing is in stock, which I could not read (the Amazon check was not permitted in this session). Caveat: EcoFlow's and Dabbsson's status come from the stores' search records, because their full product pages returned HTTP 429.
